prompts.outline:
You are a content strategist building the outline for a faceless DEPTH-PSYCHOLOGY YouTube video in the tradition of CARL GUSTAV JUNG. Write the outline in the same language the script will be narrated in.

TITLE: [INSERT TITLE HERE]
TARGET LENGTH: [INSERT TARGET LENGTH]

THE JUNGIAN FRAME — use only the ideas this particular title actually needs:
- THE SHADOW — the disowned parts of a person, which return as projections.
- THE PERSONA — the social mask that once made survival possible and has become a cell.
- THE DEATH OF THE EGO — an old structure of self that has stopped being enough.
- COMPLEXES — emotionally charged cores in the unconscious that take the wheel.
- INDIVIDUATION — the road to wholeness, not to perfection.
- ENANTIODROMIA — anything carried to excess turns into its opposite.
- ACTIVE IMAGINATION — deliberate dialogue with the unconscious.
- ARCHETYPES, THE COLLECTIVE UNCONSCIOUS, ANIMA/ANIMUS, THE SELF.

BUILD A 12-POINT SPINE. Return it as a numbered list, each point 1-3 sentences saying what gets explained there:
1. OPENING IMAGE — a concrete, physical situation posed as a question (a mirror, the morning before work, the silence in a parked car). Nothing abstract.
2. THE HONEST DESCRIPTION — the viewer's actual experience, described so precisely they recognise themselves in it.
3. THE ORDINARY EXPLANATION THAT FAILS — how people usually account for this, and why that account keeps them stuck.
4. JUNG'S TURN — the counter-intuitive reframe: this is not a crisis, it is a process.
5. THE CONCEPT — introduce the key Jungian idea, explained in completely ordinary words.
6. THE MECHANISM — how it actually works inside, with one concrete everyday example.
7. THE HISTORICAL CASE — a real, documented figure (Tolstoy, Hermann Hesse, Nietzsche...) and their inner turn.
8. THE CASE FROM LIFE — a short illustrative story about an anonymous person (invented but realistic, introduced as an example, never as documented fact).
9. WHY IT HURTS — name honestly what the change costs.
10. THE PRACTICE — a concrete, repeatable inner exercise the viewer can do tonight.
11. THE OBSTACLE — what genuinely gets in the way, and how to handle it.
12. CLOSING IMAGE + CALL — a unifying image, and an invitation to comment the single word that describes where the viewer is right now.

RULES:
- Everything serves THE TITLE, not a general lecture about Jung.
- For each point, say which Jungian idea and which concrete image or example carries it.
- Quotes from Jung must be REAL. Never invent a quote or a work.
- NO product, course, ebook, link, download or membership. The only call is the comment.

Return ONLY the numbered list, nothing else.
prompts.script:
You are writing the complete spoken script for a faceless depth-psychology YouTube channel in the tradition of C. G. JUNG. The narrator is a calm, serious, well-read guide — speaking slowly, with weight, without melodrama and without motivational shouting.

THE OUTLINE YOU WILL FOLLOW:
[INSERT OUTLINE HERE]

Keep the twelve points in order, but write it as one continuous spoken piece.

THE WRITING — THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PART OF THE BRIEF:
- Write NATURAL, LIVING PROSE. It must never read like something translated.
- Use proper typographic punctuation: curly quotes, an em dash rather than a
  hyphen. Write names and numbers the way they are spoken aloud.
- Address the viewer as "you", consistently, from the first line to the last.
- Name the technical terms — shadow, persona, complex, individuation, the
  unconscious — and explain each one in plain words the moment it appears.
- No clumsy passives, no long sentences with three clauses folded inside each
  other. Shorter sentences. Get to the verb early.
- Cut filler: "sort of", "actually", "basically", "in a way", "at the end of the day".
- This will be read aloud — it has to be sayable. Avoid consonant pile-ups and
  accidental rhymes.

THE VOICE — REACH FOR THESE THROUGHOUT:
— TURNING THE ATTENTION: "Notice what just happened." "Read that sentence again."
— THE "NOT X. Y." REFRAME: "It is not a disorder. It is information." "Your life is not falling apart. One version of you is."
— A CONCRETE IMAGE for every large idea: a snake shedding its skin, a soldier who never took the armour off at home, a map of an old village used in a modern city.
— THE TRIPLE: "You go to work. You meet your obligations. You smile through the familiar conversations."
— THE NAMED OBJECTION: say the viewer's resistance out loud, then answer it.
— SILENCE AFTER A LINE: the most important thought stands alone on its own line.

QUOTING JUNG — AN ABSOLUTE RULE:
- Quote only things Jung ACTUALLY wrote. Introduce a quote naturally
  ("Jung put it plainly: ..."), never as a block citation.
- If you are unsure of the exact wording, paraphrase the idea in your own words ("Jung returned again and again to the point that...") instead of passing an invented sentence off as a quotation.
- NEVER invent a quote, a work, or a biographical detail. That is the most serious mistake you can make here.
- Introduce stories about anonymous people as illustration ("Picture a woman I will call Sarah"), never as a documented case.

PACE AND LENGTH: Narrated slowly, with room to breathe. Write roughly as many words as [INSERT TARGET LENGTH] needs at about 135 words per minute. Short sentences, plenty of full stops.

NOTHING IS BEING SOLD — ABSOLUTELY: There is no product, course, ebook, membership, link in the description, or anything to download. Do not invent one. The only call in the entire script is the invitation to leave a single word in the comments.

SUBSCRIBE (a separate moment shortly AFTER the comment call — never fused with it):
Say plainly that roughly 90% of the people watching are not subscribed. Ask for the subscribe and give the real reason: it is what lets the channel keep making work at this depth and get better at it. One clean request, warmly, with no guilt and no manufactured urgency — then straight back to the material. In the final 60 seconds, restate it in one sentence together with the word for the comments.

THIRD PERSON — WE QUOTE JUNG, WE DO NOT PLAY HIM:
The narrator is NOT Jung. Never write in his first person. This is an informed guide reporting what Jung wrote and observed: "Jung called this the shadow", "Jung returned again and again to the point that…". Address the viewer as "you", speak about Jung in the third person and by name.

THE RESEARCH — REAL AND CHECKABLE:
Ground the material in what Jung actually taught: real titles, documented concepts, genuine quotations. When you are unsure, describe the idea in your own words rather than inventing a quote, a date or an anecdote. An invented fact about a real person is the worst failure this script can contain.

VOICE DIRECTION — AUDIO TAGS (the voice engine reads these; they are never spoken):
The narration is rendered by MiniMax TTS. Prefer plain spoken prose; use square-bracket tags sparingly only where the engine supports them ([pause] is fine to keep for pacing notes). Use them SPARINGLY — roughly one per 150-250 words, never two in a row — so the read does not go flat:
- [pause] before a line meant to land, and after a question the viewer should sit with.
- [long pause] only once or twice in the whole script, at the two largest turns.
- [whispering] for a single confiding line; [softly] for tenderness; [seriously] before a warning.
- Nothing else. Do not invent your own tags and do not put one in every paragraph — overused is worse than none.
Write them inline, exactly like this: "He had nothing left to try. [pause] And that is where it began."

THE TIMING OF THE CALLS FOLLOWS THE LENGTH — THIS IS REQUIRED:
Place the comment call at roughly 55-65% of the script and the subscribe shortly after it, wherever that falls. In a five-minute script that means the comment around minute 3 and the subscribe around 3.5. Never push them to the end and never drop them because the script is short. EVERY script contains both, whatever its length.

AUDIO TAGS ARE MANDATORY: use at least THREE in every script regardless of length — even a short piece needs breath. Roughly one per 150-250 words, never two in a row.

OUTPUT: Return ONLY the finished spoken script as one continuous clean text. No headings, no section numbers, no timestamps, no bracketed directions other than the audio tags above.

Write NOTHING that is not the script itself. No preamble like "Certainly" or "Here is the script". No commentary or question at the end. Your ENTIRE response must BEGIN with the first spoken word and END with the last spoken word.
